title: Comprehensive Behavior Modification & Cognitive Habit Architecture
description: Design an evidence-based behavioral intervention utilizing operant conditioning and cognitive reframing.
problemStatement:
Develop a comprehensive behavior modification and habit formation program to help university students eliminate chronic bedtime social media scrolling (revenge bedtime procrastination) and establish a restorative sleep routine.

### Context:
Sleep deprivation impairs neuroplasticity, memory consolidation, and emotional regulation. Overcoming this habit requires altering the environmental stimulus cues, behavioral responses, and reinforcement consequences.

### Your Objective:
Create an actionable multi-phase intervention synthesizing Operant Conditioning, Classical Stimulus Control, and Cognitive Reframing.
requirements: Perform a functional behavioral analysis identifying the antecedent environmental cues (phone on nightstand, darkness), the target behaviors, and the immediate reinforcing payoffs (dopamine bursts, stress distraction).
Apply Classical Conditioning stimulus control principles: re-associating the bed and bedroom exclusively with sleep and relaxation rather than work and screens.

Incorporate Operant Conditioning techniques: formulate a shaping ladder with successive approximations, select effective positive reinforcers, and design an intermittent reinforcement fading schedule.

Integrate Cognitive Restructuring: identify and reframe maladaptive thoughts (e.g., 'I worked hard all day, so I deserve to scroll for 2 hours') with adaptive rational thoughts that promote long-term well-being.
hints: Hint 1: Replacing an undesirable habit with a competing constructive habit (e.g., listening to an audiobook) is vastly more effective than attempting cold-turkey suppression.
Hint 2: Establish clear pre-commitment strategies (such as placing the phone in a charging station outside the bedroom).
